patients.summary: Healthy young man who joined the practice from pediatrics at 18 and started college in 2025. Infectious mononucleosis with an amoxicillin rash at student health in July 2025, then enteroviral meningitis seen in the ED in January 2026; both resolved. The practice heard of each first from him, and the outside records came late.

documents.title: New Patient Preventive Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
18 y/o M here to establish adult primary care; aged out of his pediatrician's office, family are members here. Came alone, mother joined by phone for part of the history.

No active complaints. Senior in high school, plans to start college in 2025. Feels well, sleeps ok.

PMH: nothing chronic. Peds records requested today. Per mom there is a note in his newborn history about herpes simplex exposure at birth; she doesn't know more and says it never came up again. Will see what the peds chart says.
PSH: none.
Meds: none. No supplements.
Allergies: NKDA.
FH: father with hypertension dx at 42. Mother hypothyroid since 40. No known immunodeficiency or autoimmune disease in the family.
SH: lives with parents in Easthampton. Never smoked, never vaped. Alcohol occasionally on a weekend, 1-2 drinks; we talked about it briefly. No drugs.

ROS negative across systems.

Exam: vitals as charted, well-appearing. HEENT clear, TMs normal, oropharynx without lesions. Neck supple, no nodes, thyroid normal. Heart RRR without murmur. Lungs clear bilaterally. Abdomen soft, nontender, no organomegaly. Skin without rash. Neuro grossly intact. Mood bright.

PHQ-2: 0.

Assessment / plan:
1. Adult preventive care, healthy 18 y/o. Baseline CBC and CMP, one-time lipid panel, HIV and hepatitis C screening today; he agreed to both.
2. Immunizations: mom reports everything up to date; confirm against peds records. Flu and COVID in the fall.
3. Neonatal HSV exposure, history only per family; will review in the peds records.

Recheck in about a year, or sooner for anything.

documents.title: Student Health Services Visit Note
documents.author: student health
documents.body:
UNIVERSITY STUDENT HEALTH SERVICES
Clinic visit 07/25/2025
Student: Asher Brennan, DOB 02/01/2006 (summer session resident)

Reason for visit: about a week of fever, sore throat and feeling wiped out, getting worse even with OTC pain medicine. His roommate was sick with something similar and just got over it. Around day 4 he took some amoxicillin a friend had left over, for the throat. Three days after that a rash came out over most of his body.

No past medical problems. No regular medications. Allergies: amoxicillin, maculopapular rash, felt to be non-IgE and related to mono.
Family: father HTN (age 42), mother hypothyroidism (age 40); no immunodeficiency or autoimmune disease in the family.
Social: never smoker; alcohol occasionally on weekends; college student, lives in the residence hall.

Temp 38.5 C (101.3 F).
Exam: tonsils with exudate. Tender cervical nodes on both sides. Liver edge and spleen tip both felt, mildly enlarged. Widespread maculopapular rash on trunk and limbs.

Labs today: WBC 15,000 with 20% atypical lymphocytes. ALT 70, AST 68. Monospot positive.

Impression: infectious mononucleosis. Rash after amoxicillin in the setting of mono.

Plan: rest, fluids, acetaminophen or ibuprofen for fever and throat pain. Stop the friend's amoxicillin, do not take it again. No sports or heavy lifting until cleared. Return for trouble swallowing or breathing, or belly pain on the left side. Follow up with his PCP.

Student Health Services, Physician

[Received by fax 09/30/2025 in response to records request.]

documents.title: got mono
documents.author: patient
documents.body: hey just letting you know I went to student health on friday and they said I have mono. my roommate had it. I also took some of my friend's amoxicillin before that because my throat was killing me and I broke out in a rash all over, they said not to take amoxicillin again. still really tired and my throat hurts but the rash is fading. do I need to come in?

documents.title: RE: got mono
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Hi Asher, sorry you're sick, and thanks for telling me. I've added amoxicillin to your allergy list as a rash so no one gives it to you by mistake.

Mono mostly needs time: rest, plenty of fluids, and Tylenol or ibuprofen for the fever and throat. Because mono can enlarge the spleen, please no contact sports, wrestling around, or heavy lifting for at least 4 weeks, and until I've checked you. If you get sharp pain in the left upper belly, trouble swallowing liquids, or trouble breathing, go to the ED.

Let's see you in about 3 weeks; the front desk will reach out. Can you also sign a release so we can get the student health note?

procedures.procedure: Office visit, established patient, low MDM

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
F/u mono, dx'd at student health 7/25 (we don't have their note yet, release signed today and request sent). Per pt: fever, exudative throat, tender nodes; told liver and spleen were a bit big; labs showed high white count and mildly elevated liver tests, monospot positive. Rash after a friend's amoxicillin, now on his allergy list.

Now ~4 wks out. Fever gone for 2 weeks. Throat fine. Still tires early in the afternoon but getting better each week, doing a light schedule. Eating normally. No abdominal pain. Has avoided sports and lifting.

Exam: afebrile, vitals as charted. Pharynx clear, no exudate. No cervical or axillary adenopathy. Abd soft, nontender, no hepatomegaly, spleen not palpable incl. on deep inspiration. Skin clear, rash gone.

A/P: Infectious mononucleosis, recovering. Repeat liver panel today. Fatigue can hang around for weeks; ok to ease back into normal activity, hold contact sports another couple of weeks. Freshman year starts soon, he'll pace himself. Message with results.

documents.title: Liver tests
documents.author: PCP
documents.body: Asher, your liver tests are back in the normal range (ALT 41, AST 29), down from what student health found in July. That fits with the mono settling down. You can go back to sports after the next couple of weeks. Good luck with the move-in.

documents.body: Student health note from 7/25 finally in. Matches what he told us: WBC 15k with 20% atypicals, ALT 70 / AST 68, monospot positive, mild hepatosplenomegaly on their exam, rash after amoxicillin. Follow-up LFTs here were normal.

reports.text: Indication: headache, fever, neck stiffness; prior to lumbar puncture. Technique: axial noncontrast images of the head. Findings: No intracranial hemorrhage, mass, or mass effect. Ventricles and sulci are normal in size for age. Basal cisterns are patent. Gray-white differentiation preserved. No extra-axial collection. Visualized paranasal sinuses and mastoid air cells are clear. Calvarium intact.

documents.title: Emergency Department Record
documents.author: emergency medicine
documents.body:
EMERGENCY DEPARTMENT PHYSICIAN RECORD
Arrival 01/12/2026 18:10. Discharged 01/13/2026 01:40.

CC: headache, light sensitivity, stiff neck, fever x2 days.

HPI: 19M, college student, mono last summer. Two days of headache with photophobia, neck stiffness and low fevers. More tired, nauseated, not eating much, aching all over. Several guys on his dorm floor had sore throats and felt run down over the past week. No travel, no animal contact, no drug use.

PMH: infectious mononucleosis 2025. Immunizations up to date per patient.
Meds: none.
Allergies: amoxicillin (rash).
FH: father HTN, mother hypothyroidism; no immunodeficiency or autoimmune disease.
SH: never smoker, occasional alcohol on weekends, lives in a residence hall.

Triage: T 38.1 C (100.6 F), BP 112/74, HR 92, RR 18.

Exam: awake and alert, uncomfortable, prefers the lights down. Photophobic. Nuchal rigidity present. Cranial nerves intact, strength and sensation symmetric, no focal deficit. No rash. Heart and lungs without abnormality.

ED course: CT head obtained before LP, unremarkable. LP L3-4 under sterile technique: clear fluid, opening pressure 170 mm H2O. CSF WBC 130/mm3 (92% lymphocytes), RBC 5/mm3, protein 76 mg/dL, glucose 64 mg/dL; serum glucose 98. Gram stain without organisms. CSF enterovirus PCR detected (resulted 23:30). Culture sent.

MDM: lymphocytic CSF with normal glucose ratio and no organisms on Gram stain, enterovirus PCR positive, well-appearing and nonfocal. Picture of viral meningitis; antibiotics not started. Felt better after rest and fluids, tolerating PO.

Diagnosis: enteroviral meningitis.
Disposition: home. Rest, fluids, OTC analgesics. Return for worsening headache, confusion, persistent vomiting, rash, or new weakness. PCP follow-up within 1-2 weeks.

Addendum 01/15/2026: CSF culture final, no growth.

[Received 02/09/2026 in response to records request.]

documents.title: ER last night
documents.author: patient
documents.body: I ended up in the ER last night with a horrible headache and stiff neck. they did a spinal tap and said it's viral meningitis, they said it was a virus that's going around the dorm. they sent me home at like 2am. head still hurts but better. they said to see my doctor

documents.title: RE: ER last night
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Asher, glad you got checked and that it looked viral. Viral meningitis usually clears on its own over a week or two. Rest, drink a lot, and use Tylenol or ibuprofen for the headache. If the headache gets much worse, you get confused, can't keep fluids down, or develop a rash or weakness, go back to the ED.

I'd like to see you next week. The front desk will call with a time.

documents.title: Office Visit
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
Post-ED f/u. Seen 1/12 at an outside ED with 2 days of headache, photophobia, stiff neck and fever; several dormmates sick. Per pt: CT head normal, LP done, told viral, probably enterovirus, no antibiotics, home same night. ED records not here yet; request sent today.

Headache gone since about 1/17. No fevers. Appetite back. Still a little more tired than usual, missed most of the first week of classes, back now. No visual changes, no weakness, no numbness. Neck moves freely.

Also reports flu shot at the campus clinic mid-October, added.

Exam: afebrile, vitals as charted. Alert, conversational. Neck supple, no meningismus. PERRL, EOMI, no nystagmus. CN II-XII intact. Strength 5/5 throughout, reflexes 2+ and symmetric, gait normal. LP site clean, no tenderness.

A/P: Enteroviral meningitis, clinically resolved. Fatigue should continue to improve. Back to full activity as tolerated. Note given for missed classes. Call with any return of headache or fever.

documents.title: Annual Physical
documents.author: PCP
documents.body:
20 y/o here for yearly exam, finished freshman year, living at home for the summer.

Interval: mono last July (student health), recovered, LFTs normalized in August. Enteroviral meningitis in January (ED, CSF enterovirus PCR positive), fully recovered by our visit in late January. Since then no headaches, no illnesses. Energy back to normal.
Meds: none. Allergies: amoxicillin (rash).
SH: never smoker, no vaping. Alcohol stays occasional, 1-2 on a weekend. Sleep ok most of the time.
PHQ-9: 1.

Exam: vitals as charted. Well-appearing. Oropharynx clear, tonsils normal size. No cervical adenopathy. Heart without murmur, regular. Lungs clear. Abdomen soft, no liver or spleen felt. Skin clear. Neuro nonfocal.

A/P:
- Healthy young adult. Taking mono off the active problem list, long since resolved.
- Screening done in 2024, no labs needed this year.
- Vaccines: flu in the fall, campus or here. Otherwise current per records.
- See him over winter break or sooner as needed.
